summary: Join our Natural Resource Economics and Management Training Course to master effective strategies for sustainable resource management and economic analysis.
lede: Natural resource economics and management helps professionals assess how resources are used, valued, and affected by competing demands. Designed for environmental, public-sector, utility, NGO, and industry practitioners, it supports practical choices about resource interventions when data, budgets, and stakeholder interests are constrained. Participants learn to map stakeholder dependence, compare options through valuation and cost-benefit analysis, and set indicators and plans to track results over time.
audienceIntro: This course is crafted for professionals across various sectors who are responsible for balancing natural resource use, compliance, and long-term value.
audience: Public sector staff in environment, water, agriculture
NGO program leads in conservation, livelihoods, climate
Utilities and infrastructure teams dependent on natural
Community development and stakeholder engagement practitioners
modules: Foundations of Natural Resource Economics and Management
Drivers of Degradation and Risk Pathways
Governance, Institutions, and Incentives That Actually Work
Financing Natural Resource Management and Sustainability
Monitoring, Indicators, and Proving Value Over Time
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of environmental science and economics principles, as well as experience in resource management or policy-making roles.
